To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have induced and characterized revertants of four different dominant mutations associated with the Antp complex of D. melanogaster and that these revertants localize the loci Antp, Dfd, Scx and Hu to the 84B1.2 band of polytene chromosome 3R.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the chromosomal location and genetic properties of four dominant mutations associated with the Antp gene complex.
the genetic and molecular analysis of the Antp complex.
the genetic organization of the Antennapodia complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Antp(73 b) is a gain-of-function mutation at the Antp locus, Scx(w) is a gain of function at Antp, and Dfd represents a new dominant locus just proximal and adjacent to Antp.
Antp(73 b), Scx(w), Hu and Dfd are all gain-of-function mutations at different loci in the Antennapodia complex.
Antp is the locus of three different dominant mutations (Antp(72), Scx(w)and Hu), and that a fourth, Dfd is located just proximal to the complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Antennapodia complex consists of at least three loci, Antp, Dfd and Scr, which are closely linked and are all associated with the same polytene chromosome band.
the Antp locus consists of two genes, Antp and Hu, that are separated by the Dfd locus.
we have shown that the Antp locus is a composite of at least four distinct genetic loci and that the dominant lesions are gain-of-function lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Antp gene complex is composed of at least three loci, Antp, Dfd, and Scr, and that the dominant mutations are associated with the Antp locus.
the dominant Antp alleles are not the result of a single gain of function lesion.
the Antp complex is a complex of at least three genes and that at least one of them is a dominant allele of a previously known recessive lethal gene.
